items.title: Nepal-Tibet floods: Latest developments in deadly disaster
items.summary: KATHMANDU, Nepal: More than 2,400 people are missing and at least 584 have been killed after a devastating, tsunami-like wall of water gouged a path through the border region between Nepal and Tibet, sweeping away entire villages. - RESCUERS REACH TIBET EPICENTRE - Rescuers in the autonomous Chinese region of Tibet have reached the main area wiped out by the devastating mudslide, Chinese state media reported. - MORE THAN 2,400 MISSING - Nepal's disaster authority raised sharply the number of missing to 1,924 Friday.

items.title: Thieves buy tickets before plundering necklace from Vienna museum
items.summary: VIENNA: Two men bought tickets to enter Vienna's Museum of Applied Arts (MAK) before smashing a display case, grabbing a 200-carat platinum and diamond necklace and walking away, police said Friday. Austrian media said the Van Cleef and Arpels necklace, with 673 precious stones, was worth several million dollars. The MAK museum confirmed the theft but said it would not comment while the investigation went ahead.

items.title: Media Prima newspaper printing operations return to Klang Valley from Sept 1
items.summary: KLANG: Media Prima Berhad's newspaper printing operations will return to the Klang Valley from Sept 1, aimed at improving printing and logistics efficiency and speeding up newspaper deliveries to the market. "The increased operational efficiency is expected to enable newspapers to reach the market faster and give Media Prima's newspaper publications an advantage. Luqman said the operation would also be supported by sufficient skilled personnel to ensure a smooth printing process.

items.title: Cambodia says no online scam compounds remain, experts skeptical
items.summary: PHNOM PENH: The Cambodian government has claimed a milestone in its fight against the scam industry accused of stealing billions of dollars from victims around the world, with officials saying they have eradicated all scam compounds in the country. However, criminal groups have moved to decentralised, small-scale activities, hiding in guesthouses, condominiums, rental houses, vehicles, and coffee shops, the statement said. Cambodian authorities were continuing to target those operations, it said.

items.title: Umno invites Pas leaders to 2026 general assembly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno will invite Pas' top leadership to its 2026 general assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur, scheduled for Sept 9 to 12. Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the decision was reached at the party's Supreme Council meeting last night. Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan previously said Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi was among the senior leaders invited to the party's 72nd Muktamar from Sept 2 to 5.

items.title: UiTM must remain accessible to underprivileged Bumiputera students - Sultan Sharafuddin
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah wants Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) to remain a gateway to social mobility for Malay and Bumiputera youths from low-income families and rural areas. His Royal Highness said that as UiTM grew and progressed, the target group for whom the institution was originally established should not be left behind or distanced from higher education opportunities. "That is the core spirit of UiTM's struggle that must never be lost," His Royal Highness said at the UiTM 2026 Royal Address at Dewan Konsert Seri Budiman here today.

items.title: Govt to continue upholding UiTM's role in Bumiputera development – Zambry
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The government will continue to uphold Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) as a key institution in the educational, professional and socioeconomic development of the Bumiputera community. Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the mandate and identity that formed the basis for UiTM's establishment and development would continue to be preserved by the government. "The mandate and identity that formed the basis for UiTM's establishment and development will continue to be preserved, but defending UiTM does not mean merely preserving what already exists.

items.title: Nepal floods: Change of plans saves German family of four
items.summary: KATHMANDU: A German family of four narrowly escaped death in Nepal's devastating flash floods, rescued by army helicopter after a last‑minute change of trekking plans spared them from disaster. Manuel Münch, 37, his Nepali wife, 35, and their two children aged 10 and 7 were airlifted to safety after sheltering with relatives near Trishuli Bazar for days, cut off by destroyed roads and bridges. A day later, the flood struck.

items.title: Indonesia escalates battle against fires, putrid haze
items.summary: PALANGKARAYA: Indonesia has intensified efforts to fight wildfires with cloud seeding and water bombing as thousands of people countrywide battle to breathe in the smoke and haze, officials said on Friday. More than five million people on Borneo and Sumatra islands were directly exposed to the risks of a putrid haze coming off dozens of fires across the vast archipelago, according to deputy health minister Dante Saksono Harbuwono. Some 13,500 people were treated for respiratory infections in July and August, Dante said.

items.title: Nepal-Tibet floods: 2,482 missing as death toll hits 584
items.summary: Nepal's tourism board on Friday put the number of tourists still "out of communication" at 622. The tourism board also said 121 tourists had been rescued. - NEPAL - The new Nepal Tourism Board figures Friday said that 149 Nepali tourists were among the 622 it listed as missing.

items.title: [UPDATED] Those detained for investigations must not be presumed guilty: Asyraf
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Individuals detained for investigations must not be treated as guilty before they are tried and convicted in court, Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said. Asyraf said Umno would not shield anyone involved in wrongdoing, abuse or misconduct, including its members and leaders, who must face justice through due legal process. On a separate matter, Asyraf said Umno would invite Pas' top leadership to attend the 2026 Umno General Assembly from Sept 9 to 12.

items.title: Green light for Umno state leaders to hold election talks, trust key: Asyraf
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno state leaders have been given the green light to hold talks with political parties on possible cooperation in upcoming elections. However, any agreement must be based on sincerity and trust, said Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki. "Any negotiations with political parties on cooperation in the coming elections must be based on sincerity and trust, not threats or intimidation," he told reporters after the Umno Supreme Council meeting here today.

items.title: Selangor Sultan wants UiTM academic programmes to be relevant with global changes
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah wants Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) academic programmes to always remain relevant to global changes so that graduates are competitive in an increasingly challenging job market. "UiTM's ability to produce Bumiputera professionals is no longer rhetoric, but a reality proven by clear figures," His Royal Highness said. "UiTM's relationship with industry must also be strengthened.

items.title: Tour bus driver tests positive for drugs following seven-vehicle crash
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: A tour bus driver involved in a seven-vehicle crash at the Jalan Lapangan Terbang Subang exit towards the Federal Highway here today tested positive for methamphetamine. Petaling Jaya police chief Assistant Commissioner Shamsudin Mamat said the driver would be brought before the Petaling Jaya Magistrates' Court tomorrow for a remand application. An initial urine screening test found that the driver tested positive for methamphetamine, he said.

items.title: Wawasan names 160 divisional pro-tem leaders nationwide
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) today announced 160 divisional pro-tem chiefs who will oversee the party's affairs at division and state levels nationwide. The appointments were formalised during a credential presentation ceremony here this afternoon, officiated by Wawasan secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Abdullah and attended by the party's leadership. Machang MP Wan Ahmad Fayhsal Wan Ahmad Kamal was among those appointed, taking charge as the Wawasan Machang divisional pro-tem chief.

items.title: Fresh flood threat hampers rescue of 558 missing in Tibet
items.summary: BEIJING: Risks of renewed flooding, heavy rain and roads covered in mud are complicating the search for hundreds of people missing in Tibet, two days after a deadly mudslide struck the China-Nepal border. The first rescuers reached the worst-hit site in Tibet on Friday afternoon, Chinese state media reported. Rescue operations were temporarily paused earlier on Friday due to risks of "secondary disasters" from the lake overflowing, state broadcaster CCTV said.

items.title: Iran war enters its endgame with no clear winner
items.summary: A threat by US President Donald Trump to impose crippling new sanctions on Iran faces a fundamental problem: Teheran is betting he will not take the final step to break the stalemate — aggressively enforcing secondary sanctions on the countries keeping its economy afloat, foremost among them China and India. Washington's latest measures, announced on Monday, mark a new phase in the conflict that began on Feb 28, shifting the battlefield from missiles and air strikes to Iran's oil revenues, banks and trading partners. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has said Washington will cut off the financial lifelines sustaining Iran's economy, while a US-led naval blockade restricts Teheran's oil exports and access to hard currency.

items.title: Muslims must lead by example through morality, integrity: Anwar
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM: Muslims must set the best example for society through good character, integrity, diligence and by rejecting corruption and wrongdoing, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan was also present. The Prime Minister said Muslims must also demonstrate balance in life by prioritising knowledge, faith, morality, spiritual and physical development, as well as material progress.

items.title: Nepal floods trauma 'enormous': Red Cross
items.summary: GENEVA: The Nepal-Tibet flood disaster has left an "enormous" level of trauma, the Red Cross said Friday, with early estimates suggesting 93,000 people may have been affected. Lila Pieters Yahia, the UN resident coordinator for Nepal, said drinking water was being airlifted into affected areas. The UN children's agency UNICEF, said at least 14 children were confirmed dead.

items.title: Merdeka is stronger when we stand together
items.summary: We in Malaysia celebrate National Day on the last day of the month. Our near neighbours — Singapore and Indonesia — also commemorate their respective independence days in August. Thus, for smaller nations like ours, it is also worth pondering how interdependence — especially among near neighbours — may actually hold the key towards preserving our independence, moving forward.

items.title: NST Leader: The sand racket digging Malaysia deeper
items.summary: Unlike contrabands like drugs, wildlife and fake luxury products, illegal sand mining barely gets any press. Illegal sand is cheaper. Nevertheless, illegal sand mining is risky.

items.title: MetMalaysia forecasts thunderstorms, rain and haze on national day
items.summary: Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and Labuan are expected to experience haze throughout the day. In Sabah, thunderstorms and rain are expected to hit the interior and Sandakan throughout the day, while Tawau is expected to experience thunderstorms in the morning and rain at night. The west coast of Sabah, meanwhile, is expected to experience haze throughout the day.

items.title: [UPDATED] Boy, 5, dies after being allegedly slashed in Sibu
items.summary: Sibu district police chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad said a man in his late 40s, believed to be a relative of the victim, has been detained to assist in investigations. "So far, we have conducted preliminary investigations at the scene," he briefly told reporters. Police are expected to issue a further statement once preliminary investigations are completed.

items.title: Teacher faces 10 charges of sexually assaulting female pupils
items.summary: The 56-year-old accused appeared before Judge Musyiri Peet at the Mukah Sessions Court today. The accused posted bail. Meanwhile, Mukah police chief Deputy Superintendent Muhamad Rizal Alias said the accused was teaching at the primary school when the alleged offences occurred.

items.title: National Day 2026 Prime Minister's address ceremony set for 2pm at PICC
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The 2026 National Day Prime Minister's Address Ceremony at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) here has been scheduled for 2pm, according to the Ministry of National Unit. "The 2026 National Day Prime Minister's 2026 Address Ceremony is an important platform to reflect on the aspirations and hopes of the Madani government leadership in fuelling the spirit of independence, strengthening patriotism, and nurturing a sense of love and responsibility towards the country. The National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) 2026 Celebration Working Committee under the Ministry of Communications had earlier announced that the Prime Minister's address ceremony had been moved from Dataran Merdeka, Kuala Lumpur to PICC due to the current haze conditions.

items.title: Teo denies allegations of involvement in gang-related activities
items.summary: KULAI: Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching today denied allegations circulating on social media linking her to gang-related activities in the state and a road accident currently under police investigation. The DAP national vice-chairman said the allegations were false and baseless, stressing that new social media accounts had been created specifically to make accusations against her. "The police, including the Johor police chief, have already held a press conference and announced that 13 suspects had been arrested.

items.title: [UPDATED] 36 M'sians in Tibet reported safe, status still being verified: Wisma Putra
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Thirty-six Malaysians in Tibet, China have reported to be safe following flash floods and landslides in the China-Nepal border area. Foreign Ministry deputy secretary-general (Bilateral Relations) Datuk Syed Mohamad Hasrin Tengku Hussin said that the identities and status of the 36 Malaysians were still being verified with Chinese authorities, and they are cross-checking for any overlap with the list of Malaysians who remained uncontactable in Nepal. The Foreign Ministry's Operations Room in Putrajaya would continue to operate round the clock to coordinate information, assist Malaysians in the affected areas and provide the latest updates to family members, Syed Mohamad Hasrin said, adding that they would continue seeking confirmation from Chinese authorities regarding the whereabouts and safety of Malaysians in Tibet before drawing any further conclusions.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - August 28, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Here are today's biggest stories: Form Six aid Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Form Six students will receive allowances, with allocations included in the 2027 Budget after dialogue with pre‑university students. Find my mum Dharaniya Rajan appealed for help to find her mother, S. Gomathi, after losing contact during Nepal's devastating flash floods on Wednesday morning. Saravanan on trial Former Human Resources Minister M. Saravanan pleaded not guilty to three charges of accepting RM1.097m in bribes to approve foreign worker quotas.

items.title: Bird-cage rooms and rooftop dorms expose Malaysia’s migrant housing enforcement gaps
items.summary: Yet, what would normally be considered adequate accommodation for a family of five is home to 15 migrant workers. Some have also resorted to constructing makeshift rooms, where space permits, on the rooftops of shop lots to accommodate foreign workers, particularly those employed in restaurants and supermarkets, and as general workers. Workers from Myanmar, Vietnam and Cambodia interviewed by Bernama said they did not mind living under such conditions.

items.title: Oriental Kopi's Q3 net profit dips 5pct to RM17mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Oriental Kopi Holdings Bhd's net profit fell five per cent to RM17 million in the third quarter (Q3) ended June 30, 2026 from RM17.95 million a year earlier. According to its filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company's revenue rose 34.2 per cent to RM156.63 million from RM116.75 million last year. For the nine months period (9M2026), Oriental Kopi's net profit increased 9.4 per cent to RM49.08 million from RM44.86 million last year, while revenue surged 39 per cent to RM443.08 million from RM317.75 million previously.

items.title: Wisma Putra: Two Malaysians found safe after Nepal floods, 55 remain unreachable
items.summary: Foreign Ministry Deputy Secretary-General (Bilateral Affairs) Datuk Syed Mohamad Hasrin Tengku Hussin said the two Malaysians had been successfully located, but their information and details were still undergoing cross-checking and further verification. Syed Mohamad Hasrin said the figure of 55 was still subject to further verification based on information received from Nepalese authorities and relevant agencies. “The official is assisting in coordinating information, monitoring developments and liaising with the relevant Nepalese authorities,” he said.

items.title: ‘False and baseless’: Teo Nie Ching rejects social media claims linking her to Johor gang activity, lodges police report
items.summary: KULAI, Aug 28 — Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching today denied allegations circulating on social media linking her to gang-related activities in the state and a road accident currently under police investigation. The DAP national vice-chairman said the allegations were false and baseless, stressing that new social media accounts had been created specifically to make accusations against her. “The police, including the Johor police chief, have already held a press conference and announced that 13 suspects had been arrested.

items.title: Stulang assemblyman Andrew Chen returns to lead Johor Opposition after bruising state election
items.summary: KULAI, Aug 28 — Johor Pakatan Harapan (PH) has agreed to appoint Stulang state assemblyman Andrew Chen Kah Eng as Johor’s Leader of the Balancing Force (Ketua Pengimbang). Johor DAP chairman Teo Nie Ching said the appointment had been agreed by all three PH component parties: DAP, PKR and Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah). In the 16th Johor state election held on July 11, Barisan Nasional formed the new state government after winning 48 seats, while PH secured eight.

items.title: Johari Abdul calls for diplomacy to prevent Cambodia-Thailand dispute from straining Asean
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Dialogue and diplomacy must continue to be prioritised in addressing the Cambodia-Thailand border issue to ensure regional peace and stability, said Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul. Johari said the border issue was among the matters discussed during his meeting with Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet on the sidelines of the Second Inter-Parliamentary Speakers’ Conference (ISC-2) in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. “Developments along the Cambodia-Thailand border were also among the matters given attention.

items.title: Thunderstorms may offer temporary haze relief as Sarawak braces for prolonged dry spell, says MetMalaysia state director
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 28 — Thunderstorms that have swept parts of Sarawak in recent days may bring temporary relief from the haze, but the improvement is unlikely to last if hot and dry conditions persist and smoke sources remain active, said Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) Sarawak director Khairul Najib Ibrahim. He said thunderstorms were a normal occurrence in tropical countries but could develop rapidly when atmospheric conditions became highly unstable. “This high daytime heat, combined with Sarawak’s natural humidity, has created highly unstable atmospheric conditions,” he said.

items.title: Zetrix AI denies any link to ex-minister Saravanan after graft charges
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Zetrix AI Group Bhd has denied any involvement or association with the former Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri M. Saravanan following rumours linking the company to the graft charges brought against him today. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said it understood that unfounded rumours or speculation linking it to Saravanan may have contributed to the recent trading activity in its shares. Zetrix AI ended the day’s trading at 59.5 sen, with 1.05 billion shares traded.

items.title: Power without trust becomes greed, warns Selangor Sultan
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 28 — Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah has urged Muslims to shun betrayal of trust, warning that it can erode public confidence and undermine the well-being of society. Sultan Sharafuddin said true independence also begins with the ability to free oneself from destructive impulses, including greed, temptation and betrayal. Raja Muda of Selangor Tengku Amir Shah Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah was also present.

items.title: SPAN: One dam critical, nine at warning level as El Nino puts pressure on Malaysia’s raw water reserves
items.summary: The National Water Services Commission (SPAN) said two dams — Jus Dam, Melaka and Labong Dam, Johor — were at the alert level, nine at the warning level and one — Sungai Pagar Dam in Labuan — at the critical level. “Dams at the warning level include Muda Dam and Ahning Dam in Kedah; Upper Layang Dam, Lower Layang Dam, Lebam Dam, Gunung Pulai 1 Dam, Gunung Pulai 2 Dam and Pontian Kechil Dam in Johor, as well as Timah Tasoh Dam in Perlis. The measures being considered are optimising the use of raw water resources, coordinating dam and WTP operations, activating alternative water sources depending on requirements, monitoring water supply demand in high-risk areas, and implementing scheduled water supply if the raw water situation continues to deteriorate.

items.title: Anwar extends condolences to Opposition Leader Hamzah Zainudin over mother’s death
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended his condolences to Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin on the passing of his mother, Mariam Kassim. In a post on X today, Anwar said he and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, prayed that Hamzah and the entire family would be given the strength and fortitude to cope with the loss. Salam takziah buat Ketua Pembangkang, Dato' Seri Hamzah Zainudin atas pemergian ibu tercinta, Allahyarhamah Hajah Mariam Kassim.

items.title: Five-year-old dies in alleged slashing incident in Sibu, police investigate
items.summary: Sibu police chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad, when contacted, confirmed the case. The suspect is believed to be in police custody to assist investigations. Further details are awaited from police.

items.title: Pahang seeks long-term solution to shallow stretches of Sungai Pahang
items.summary: Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said the state government is currently obtaining a complete report from relevant parties on the condition of the river before further action can be decided. He said the report is important to enable the state government to identify the most suitable methods, including the implementation of short-term, medium-term, and long-term measures to address the issue. Meanwhile, Wan Rosdy said the implementation of the pipe replacement programme to address water supply issues and the development of energy infrastructure projects continues to be a priority for the Pahang government in strengthening basic facilities and accelerating the state’s development.

items.title: Mapim to deploy humanitarian mission to Nepal on Sept 5
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 28 — The Malaysian Consultative Council of Islamic Organisations (Mapim) will deploy a humanitarian mission to Nepal on September 5 to assist victims affected by massive flash floods in the country. Mapim president Mohd Azmi Abdul Hamid said the organisation had contacted the Embassy of Nepal to obtain an initial overview of the situation. “To maximise the impact of the assistance, Mapim is also inviting participation from other local non-governmental organisations (NGOs), including a collaboration with humanitarian organisation MyCare, alongside two local NGOs in Nepal,” he told a press conference on the Regional Mosques Conference 2026 here today.

items.title: ‘After we shout ‘Merdeka’, don’t leave rubbish everywhere’: SWCorp warns revellers
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 28 — The Solid Waste and Public Cleansing Management Corporation (SWCorp) will step up monitoring and enforcement by deploying enforcement personnel at key locations during the National Day celebrations. The Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) said in a statement today that enforcement action would be taken against individuals found committing littering offences in public places throughout the celebrations. “The public is reminded that littering in public places is an offence that may be subject to action under the Solid Waste and Public Cleansing Management Act 2007,” the statement said.

items.title: ‘Why restrain them?’ Anwar says students must be free to speak, think critically
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 28 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said young Malaysians should be allowed to speak freely and think critically rather than be controlled. He said those aged 18 and above were already entitled to vote, so they should be allowed to discuss issues and express their views. Let them discuss,” he said.

items.title: MoH warns against ‘weight-loss pens’ containing unapproved Retatrutide
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 28 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) has warned the public against buying or using ‘weight-loss pens’ claimed to contain Retatrutide or Reta, as no products containing the drug are registered for use in Malaysia. In a statement today, MOH said Retatrutide remains an investigational drug currently undergoing Phase 3 clinical trials. “As of August 17, 2026, no product containing Retatrutide has been registered with the Drug Control Authority (DCA) for use in Malaysia.

items.title: ‘I must do something’: Wife of missing Malaysian firefighter flies to Nepal to seek answers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — The wife of a Fire and Rescue Department Special Air Unit officer, who was reported missing in Nepal, flew to Kathmandu today to seek an update on the search for her husband. Hani Othman said she had decided to travel to Nepal alone to get the latest updates on efforts to find those missing there, saying she did not want to stay at home. Hani’s husband, Fire and Rescue Department Senior Fire Officer II Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, in his 40s, better known as Loe, was reported missing during a climbing expedition in Nepal.

items.title: Malaysia, Indonesia step up haze response with weather modification plans
items.summary: JAKARTA, Aug 28 — Indonesia has confirmed it is coordinating with Malaysia to tackle transboundary haze, with the first order of business being weather modification operations along border areas. National Disaster Mitigation Agency (BNPB) Data, Information, and Disaster Communication Centre Acting Head, Berton Panjaitan, said the two sides are currently discussing wider efforts to address the haze situation. Berton said Malaysia had also conveyed its readiness to help in firefighting efforts.

items.title: Teacher charged with 10 counts of sexually assaulting pupils in Mukah
items.summary: MUKAH, Aug 28 — A 56-year-old teacher has been charged in the Mukah Magistrate’s Court today with 10 counts of sexually assaulting female pupils between 2022 and 2024. Mukah police chief DSP Muhamad Rizal Alias said the accused, who was a teacher at a primary school here at the time of the alleged offences, was accused of committing the offences against 10 girls while in a position of trust as their teacher. Rizal said a police report was lodged by a secondary school counselling teacher in Mukah on August 7 after receiving a complaint from one of the alleged victims.

items.title: Anwar: Budget 2027 to include allowance for Form Six students
items.summary: SEBERANG PERAI, Aug 28 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he will be including an allowance for Form Six students under Budget 2027, which is due to be tabled in October. He said the government decided this after feedback from pre-university students who noted that there was no government allowance for those in Form Six. “So in our Budget this October, I will include an allocation and allowance for Form Six students,” he said.

items.title: Anwar tells schools, varsities: Zero tolerance for bullying, arrogance
items.summary: SEBERANG PERAI, Aug 28 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today urged schools and higher education institutions to show zero tolerance towards bullying as such behaviour could undermine the country’s future. Anwar said academic achievement alone could not build a civilised nation without values, character and respect for others. The prime minister said students who bully, belittle or humiliate others could not be allowed to become future leaders.

items.title: MetMalaysia: Haze expected to persist across Sarawak tomorrow, with thunderstorms in several areas
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 28 — Haze is expected to persist across all divisions in Sarawak tomorrow (August 29), with isolated thunderstorms and rain forecast in several areas, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia). The department’s weather forecast said haze is expected statewide in the morning, affecting Sri Aman, Betong, Bintulu, Kapit, Kuching, Miri, Mukah, Samarahan, Sarikei, Serian, Sibu and Limbang. In the afternoon, thunderstorms are forecast in a few places in Kuching, Kapit, Miri and Limbang, while haze is expected to continue in Sri Aman, Betong, Bintulu, Mukah, Samarahan, Sarikei, Serian and Sibu.

items.title: In Sarawak, Jalan Lapangan Terbang junction to close overnight for works from Aug 28 to 29
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 28 — The junction from Jalan Lapangan Terbang to Lorong Lapangan Terbang 1, near the voco hotel, will be temporarily closed overnight from Friday at 10pm until Saturday at 5am for sheet-piling dismantling works. Sarawak Metro Sdn Bhd, in a statement on Friday, advised road users to use alternative routes and plan their journeys accordingly during the closure. — The Borneo Post pic Alternative route to Lorong Lapangan Terbang 1.

items.title: Anwar: Malaysia coordinating aid to Nepal, may deploy Smart elite rescuers
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Aug 28 — Malaysia is coordinating the delivery of aid to Nepal following the devastating floods in the country, including the possibility of deploying the Malaysian Special Search and Rescue Team (Smart), said Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Yesterday, the Prime Minister instructed all relevant departments, including MKN, and the Foreign Ministry, to immediately identify and contact Malaysians affected by the disaster. Earlier, the Foreign Ministry said 57 Malaysians remained uncontactable following yesterday’s floods at the Nepal-Tibet border areas.

items.title: Odd-job worker, cook each jailed 10 years, caned two strokes for sexually assaulting teen girl in Kuching
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 28 — The Sessions Court has sentenced a 22-year-old oddjobber and a 20-year-old cook to 10 years in prison and six strokes of the cane each for sexually assaulting a teenage girl. Oddjobber Daniel Arrazy Salmi Abdullah also received an additional three-year prison term for possessing child sexual abuse material. Investigations also led to the arrest of the oddjobber that same night to assist with investigations into the sexual assault case.

items.title: Sri Aman records Sarawak’s worst air quality at 4pm as API hits 215
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 28 — Sri Aman recorded Sarawak’s worst air quality today, with its Air Pollutant Index (API) reaching 215 at 4pm, placing the district in the very unhealthy category. The reading, recorded by the Air Pollutant Index of Malaysia (APIMS), was the highest among monitoring stations across the state, with Sri Aman the only area in Sarawak to record an API reading above 200. Sibu recorded an API reading of 151, Bintulu 136, Miri 99 and Samalaju 99, while ILP Miri recorded 87, Mukah 87, Limbang 72 and Kapit 71.

items.title: Sarawak’s Long Banga, Ba Kelalan STOLports to be upgraded this year with RM30m allocation
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 28 — Work to upgrade the Long Banga and Ba Kelalan STOLports is expected to begin this year following the federal government’s approval of RM30 million for the two rural air facilities. Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah said RM15 million had been allocated for each STOLport under the Airport Development Fund. He said the upgrades would include terminal improvements and, where feasible, runway extensions based on site conditions.

items.title: LSH Infra-Pertama Makmur JV win job for Bandar Malaysia-Seri Kembangan elevated highway project
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 28 — LSH Infra Sdn Bhd and Pertama Makmur Sdn Bhd Joint Venture has been awarded the proposed development of the Bandar Malaysia-Seri Kembangan Elevated Highway (BSE), a strategic infrastructure project aimed at strengthening connectivity and easing traffic congestion in Greater Kuala Lumpur. He said the BSE, envisaged as a high-capacity connecting route, would integrate several major highway networks to improve connectivity across Greater Kuala Lumpur. “This includes the Kuala Lumpur-Seremban Expressway, Maju Expressway (MEX), Sungai Besi Expressway (BESRAYA), New Pantai Expressway (NPE), Shah Alam Expressway (KESAS) and the Kuala Lumpur Traffic Dispersal System (SPRINT) network.

items.title: Upside-down Jalur Gemilang, Perak flag: Perak MCA apologises, staff quits
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Perak MCA has apologised to the Sultan of Perak and Malaysians over the upside-down display of the Jalur Gemilang and Perak flag at its state headquarters in Ipoh, which went viral on social media today. Perak MCA state liaison committee chairman Datuk Dr Mah Hang Soon said the party took full responsibility and viewed the incident seriously, Kosmo! “The incident occurred this morning when an elderly staff member at the Perak MCA state headquarters was tasked with installing and putting up the Jalur Gemilang and Perak flag to mark National Month.

items.title: ‘We have to accept whatever comes’: Family of Bomba special forces officer missing in Nepal stays positive
items.summary: SIK, Aug 28 — The family of Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, 44, a member of the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department’s (JBPM) special forces team, who remains missing following the flash floods and landslide in Rasuwa, Nepal, is holding onto hope that he and his companions will be found safe. His brother, Mohd Saiful Munir Mohd Isa, 46, said the family is choosing to stay positive and believes the communication blackout is due to the disaster that has struck the area. Mohd Saiful Munir said the family does not see Loe’s trip to Nepal as unusual, given that his brother is deeply passionate about climbing and frequently travels abroad for climbing activities.
